comments.text:
At the 6500XT's price, I would suggest a used 2060 or 5700XT as long as they aren't obvious mining cards. All the budget cards have their really obvious flaws this generation. The 6500XT and the A380 need PCIe 4.0 (And Re-Bar for the latter, though I can't think of a set-up that has 4.0 without Re-Bar support.) to perform optimally. The 6400 is too pricey for what it is and what it can't do. The 1650 is three years old and still overpriced. The 1630 is the worst card I've seen in a long time. 

Though if you do encode/transcode a lot of videos in H265/AV1, the A380 is a legitimately great choice. Otherwise, it's the best of a bad lot. Intel has really gone a long way towards fixing launch day performance. Most of the DX9 issues you see in these reviews have been fixed by DXVK being implemented. The problem is that all these budget cards are about to get trounced by developers finally utilizing 9th-gen consoles to their potential. None of them will be able to run titles post-2023 at 1080p30 on low settings if some of these minimum specs are to be believed.

There were a few listings a while back for 8GB 6500XTs, but I have no idea how they perform.
